newsitem.title: LEBANON: Five killed in mounting south Lebanon violence.
newsitem.headline: Five killed in mounting south Lebanon violence.

text.p: Five Lebanese were killed on Thursday by two bombs and Israeli shelling as south Lebanon slid deeper into the worst violence since an Israeli offensive more than a year ago.

The latest deaths included a woman and her two children killed by a roadside bomb planted by unknown assailants, a pro-Israeli militiaman killed by a bomb planted in his car by Hizbollah guerrillas and a farmer killed by retaliatory Israeli shelling.

It raised the toll to 13 dead -- including seven civilians -- since Monday, when Israel began the latest round of violence by killing five guerrillas of the Islamic movement Hizbollah (Party of God) with a roadside bomb.

Hizbollah had also unleashed salvos of rockets at Israeli army targets near the border on Wednesday night. There were no casualties and it was unclear if any hit Israel, but many people in northern Israel spent the night in shelters.

The violence on the last active Arab war front with Israel came amid deepening world concern about prospects for Middle East peace because of the Israeli-Palestinian confrontation triggered by a twin suicide bomb attack against Jews in Jerusalem.

Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of exporting domestic problems by carrying out attacks in south Lebanon and warned that the violence could spread.
Bouez said U.S. ambassador to Lebanon Richard Jones had telephoned him and expressed Washington's concern. "We share this concern," Bouez said.

The violence this week is the worst since a month-long Israeli onslaught against Hizbollah in April 1996 ended with an agreement that neither side would target civilians. Most of the 200 Lebanese killed in that air and artillery offensive were civilians.
In addition to the four Lebanese civilians killed on Thursday, on Tuesday two old men were killed by Israeli rockets and another civilian man died from a roadside bomb planted by unknown assailants.
Pro-Israeli militia sources said the bomb in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone on Thursday that killed the woman and her children had seriously wounded the man driving their car.
The bomb exploded near Markaba in the eastern sector of the Israeli-held zone. Sheikh Nabeel Qaawook, Hizbollah's political leader in southern Lebanon, blamed the bomb on Israeli forces.
Earlier in the day, a pro-Israeli Lebanese militiaman was killed by a bomb planted in his car. In Beirut, a Hizbollah spokesman claimed responsibility.
That attack triggered heavy Israeli shelling which killed one Lebanese civilian and wounded two, security sources said.

Israeli troops have been in southern Lebanon since 1978 and in 1985 set up the current 15-km (nine-mile) deep occupation zone to protect its northern border. Hizbollah is fighting to drive the Israelis and their local militia allies from the zone.

Five members of the U.N. peacekeeping mission that has been based in south Lebanon since 1978 trying to restore government control died on Wednesday night when their helicopter crashed in the Israeli-occupied zone.
Italian investigators arrived on Thursday but a U.N. spokesman said they would be unlikely to see the wreckage and establish the cause of the crash before Friday afternoon.
Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi was flying to Tel Aviv for a memorial service for the dead peacekeepers on Thursday and then on to Beirut, U.N. officials said.
